chunks: And from his sayings (peace be upon him): When Allah the Exalted gave him victory over the companions of the Camel,
one of his companions said to him, 'I wish my so-and-so brother had been with you as a witness to see what Allah granted you victory over your enemies with,'
whereupon he (peace be upon him) said to him:

key_terms.أَصْحَابِ الْجَمَل: The Companions of the Camel (referring to the battle participants)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say after his victory at the Battle of Jamal when a companion wished his brother had been there to witness it?
ai.summary: This narration from Nahj al-Balagha captures the humility of Imam Ali (AS) following the Battle of Jamal, where he responded to a companion's wish for a relative to witness his victory. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on divine favor (tawfiq) being a result of piety rather than mere military prowess, reflecting the spiritual dimension of the conflict against the Ahl al-Bukht. The exchange highlights the personal and communal significance of the battle in establishing Ali's legitimacy and the nature of his leadership.

en.sayed-ali-raza: When [1] Allāh gave him (Amīr al-mu’minīn) victory over the enemy at the Battle of Jamal
one of his comrades said on that occasion, “I wish my brother so-and-so had been present and he too would have seen what success and victory Allāh had given you,”
